instrument: Kalshi: CPI inflation above 3.5% for the twelve months ending September 2026

catalyst.event: BLS releases the September 2026 CPI on 2026-10-14 at 08:30 ET; the contract closes 2026-10-14 12:29 UTC. It resolves YES only if the one-decimal headline CPI-U year-over-year prints 3.6% or higher - the rule is "increases by more than 3.5%", so a 3.5% print resolves NO.
catalyst.action: Buy NO at 18c or better. This is a hold-to-resolution position with a defined maximum loss of the premium; size it as such and do not add on adverse moves.

thesis: The market prices an 82.5% chance the September headline prints 3.6% or above. That requires a specific arithmetic outcome: with the August NSA index at 334.980 and September 2025 at 324.800, a 3.6% print needs September month-over-month NSA inflation of +0.403% or hotter. Across the twelve Septembers from 2014 to 2025 the NSA month-over-month averaged +0.181% and cleared +0.403% exactly once, in 2017 on the Harvey and Irma gasoline spike, and 2026 is running colder than 2025 rather than hotter - June through August came in at -0.349%, -0.010% and +0.318%, averaging -0.014% against +0.260% for the same months a year ago.
key_risk: There is no stop; the maximum loss is the full 18c premium and the position is decided in a single data release. The specific way it loses is a one-month shock the seasonal record cannot see - a September energy spike, a shelter reset, or tariff pass-through concentrated into one print. Note also that the ladder is thin: 1,035 contracts of 24-hour volume against 39,106 of open interest, so the 17/18 quote may not absorb size and the fill matters.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is simply that a market with 39,106 contracts of open interest is unlikely to be 45 points wrong about a government statistic, and that I am extrapolating a seasonal from twelve observations into an inflation regime that has not looked like those twelve years - 2026 has already delivered monthly NSA prints of +1.049% and +0.850%. Answered on the direction of travel rather than the level: headline year-over-year has fallen from 4.249% in May to 3.531%, 3.365% and 3.397%, and the one input that could deliver a hot September is going the other way, with XLE -7.0% off its high and OXY -2.07% on 2026-09-29. The residual is real, which is why the claim is 60% and not 85%.

evidence.detail: Fetched from the contract record: close_time 2026-10-14T12:29:00Z, expiration 2027-01-13, settlement source Bureau of Labor Statistics. The rules text confirms resolution on the one-decimal-place BLS value and the strict "more than 3.5%" threshold. The event is listed on Robinhood Prediction Markets as "Inflation in September 2026 (CPI YoY)".

Method shown in full. FRED CPIAUCNS: August 2026 = 334.980, September 2025 = 324.800. September 2026 YoY = 334.980 x (1 + m/m) / 324.800 - 1. A 3.6% print needs YoY >= 3.55%, hence m/m >= +0.403%. At the twelve-year September seasonal mean of +0.181% the YoY is 3.32% and prints 3.3; at a repeat of September 2025 (+0.254%) it is 3.397% and prints 3.4. Both resolve NO.

The market-knows-better case is answered with the fetched ladder and the fetched trend. The full ladder implies P(print >= 3.2) 98%, 3.3 97%, 3.4 95%, 3.5 91%, 3.6 82.5%, 3.7 43%, 3.8 11.5%, 3.9 3% - i.e. it assigns 5% to any print at or below the twelve-year seasonal outcome. Against that, headline YoY has decelerated 4.249% -> 3.531% -> 3.365% -> 3.397% from May to August, and the energy complex that produced the single exceptional September in the record is falling rather than spiking.
